summary: Draft updated at submission.json (validated read-only: valid, no diagnostics) with the harness assurance_generated_test.go; scratch removed. This turn contributes a source-explained negative result that grounds the counterevidence of the empty-Entries read-index finding: the response direction of the same message family is validated while the request direction is not. New child question @readindex_response_validation (parent 486d1abb02d149b084c6a6800b992c97-question-1) with a sourced Behaviour entry and an experiment: stepFollower requires exactly one entry in MsgReadIndexResp, logging an error and returning for any other count, and only appends a ReadState for the single-entry shape (raft.go:1766-1771). The harness steps zero-entry, two-entry and one-entry responses into a real follower of an elected three-voter cluster, with panics recovered and read states measured, and three comparisons declare what must hold: no read state for zero entries, none for two entries, and exactly one read state carrying the request context for the control. Construction-time local runs show, for the record and not as formal evidence, that malformed responses are dropped with no panic and no read state (read_states_added 0 in both cases) while the well-formed response is accepted with index 7 and request context 'assurance-rctx' (read_states_added 1), which is the contrast that makes the request direction's unchecked Entries[0] access stand out. Limitations state that the responses are stepped directly into the follower, that the Node layer's response filtering and the transport are not exercised, and that the probe covers shape validation only, not whether an accepted response corresponds to an issued request; the formal conclusion awaits the controller's retained receipt.
